gen-dafont-groovy-gf-lisu-bosa: Lisu Bosa reads sturdy and large, its counters spilling out into the surrounding space with a gently tempered contrast. Groovy delivers the funk; Lisu Bosa does the talking.
gen-dafont-impact-label-gf-halant: Halant brings a faint but real thick-thin shift and outward-pointing terminals, with a towering x-height like a stubby pencil stroke. Halant keeps things traditional below, while Impact Label stamps its separate, heavy letters above.
gen-dafont-impact-label-gf-hedvig-letter: Impact Label hits hard, each heavy letter a bead on a rod. Hedvig Letters Serif follows with open-ended curves and a sturdy, medium-contrast body, so the heavy heading feels braced by something authoritative.
gen-dafont-impact-label-gf-noto-serif-he: Blunt and heavy, Impact Label spaces its letters apart like beads on a rod. But Noto Serif Hentaigana stays refined, its open curves showing subtle modulation beside the heading's shout.
gen-dafont-jelly-crazies-gf-domine: Playful and wobbly, Jelly Crazies nearly seals its bowls shut, while Domine keeps a breathing space inside every curve. Paragraphs set in Domine would read dignified, measured and refined.
gen-dafont-jelly-crazies-gf-faustina: Wobbly and playful, Jelly Crazies draws its bowls almost shut with no calligraphic thinning. Yet Faustina brings authority, its open-jawed c like pliers and its bowls thinning gracefully.
gen-dafont-jelly-crazies-gf-halant: Halant carries authority in its outward-pointing terminals and moderate stem-to-hairline ratio, a steady lettering-pen feel against Jelly Crazies. And a full page of Halant would feel traditional and grounded, never wobbling.
gen-dafont-jelly-crazies-gf-headland-one: Jelly Crazies wobbles along in wire-like lines with nearly sealed bowls. Headland One then reads in traditional, dignified fashion, its letters spaced well apart and its stroke weight shifting only gently.
gen-dafont-jelly-crazies-gf-hedvig-lette: Playful from the very first wobble, Jelly Crazies keeps its bowls nearly closed. Hedvig Letters Serif offers open-ended curves, sturdy lowercase and medium-key contrast, sounding authoritative and classic.
gen-dafont-jelly-crazies-gf-lisu-bosa: Jelly Crazies moves with stems and arcs in wobbly lockstep. Lisu Bosa gives it sturdy, editorial footing, with counters spilling into the space and a medium-low contrast that quiets the wobble.
